evals.prompt: I put together our household budget in House_Budget.xlsx. Before I send it to my partner, can you check it for mistakes? Just tell me what's actually wrong and what I should fix.
evals.expected_output: Runs the audit, checks the four FORMULA_DRIFT findings in context, reports House Budget!F123 as the one real formula mistake with the right fix, and lists the other three as fine by design. The workbook is unchanged.
expectations: The answer says House Budget!F123 is wrong because it sums column G (G65:G122) instead of the Total Spent column F
The fix given for F123 is =SUM(F65:F122) or equivalent, not a row sum such as =SUM(G123:AE123)
The answer does not tell the user to change House Budget!C10 (the Total Income line)
The answer does not tell the user to change 'Money In Checking Next Month'!E61 (Total Left) or L2 (Total Tax)
The answer says the values were not recalculated (cached values only)
House_Budget.xlsx has the same SHA-256 after the run as before

evals.prompt: Audit Q3_Forecast.xlsx and tell me what's wrong with it. Write the report to audit_report.md and produce an annotated copy.
evals.expected_output: Writes audit_report.md and an annotated copy at a new path, leaves Q3_Forecast.xlsx untouched, and explains the seeded defects once per cell, with fixes, plus the checks that could not run because the file has no cached values.
expectations: audit_report.md exists and contains the non-certification disclaimer
An annotated workbook exists at a path other than Q3_Forecast.xlsx
Q3_Forecast.xlsx has the same SHA-256 after the run as before
Budget!B10 is explained once, as a January total that stops before the Marketing row (B9), not once per rule
Budget!B6 is explained as counting B5 twice
Budget!B14 (#REF!) is presented as needing the user's input on the intended range, not repaired by guesswork
The answer says the value-dependent checks (cached totals, cross-foot) did not run because the workbook has no cached values or recalculation was unavailable

evals.prompt: I inherited Ops_Tracker.xlsx from a colleague who left. Can I trust the numbers in it? Give me the top issues in plain English, most important first.
evals.expected_output: Leads with the live errors (#VALUE! in Q9:Q11, #REF! in I10:I11) and their causes, folds the 31 hidden-structure findings into one point about hidden helper columns, does not call C5 an error, and states the coverage limits in plain language.
expectations: The top issues include the #VALUE! errors in formamspnc (7)!Q9:Q11
The top issues include the #REF! errors in formamspnc (7)!I10:I11
The hidden-column findings appear as one point, not as a list of separate items
formamspnc (7)!C5 is not presented as an error
The answer says the audit used cached values without recalculation
Rule IDs such as FORMULA_DRIFT are not the main vocabulary of the answer
